question: Does the sham yaw originate in the physical body, in its neural command, or in the asymmetric PN output adapter?

rivals.A: The left-only 629-general-destination PN output substitution contributes materially to the DNb05 and yaw asymmetry; turn off only this substitution in a prospective organism child, retaining 466 dynamic destinations and native anatomy.
rivals.B: Downstream central convergence or thresholds suppress DNa02 while preserving a DNb05 command; extend the in-kernel FP64 tap to DNb05 and compare effective targets and numerical reference before lesion selection.
rivals.C: Sham yaw reflects a basal DNb05 command, physical posture/inertia, or both; replay the logged sham command on the same body state and compare open-loop zero and equal opposite commands.

first_prototype: C body-only physical replay from the exact 40-ms prepared sham body/controller snapshot, 400 ms at 25-us MuJoCo substeps, using the unchanged contact controller and numerical body. Replay saved sham commands first; then zero,+0.2,-0.2 deg/s with forward command 0.2 mm/s. This is a body/device diagnostic, never an organism or stage-3 PASS.
control_gates: Saved sham command replay must match the complete-organism qpos and qvel trace to 1e-8 max absolute and yaw to 1e-6 degrees before interpreting open-loop tests; all arms start from independently restored identical body/controller state. Preserve failures.
stop: Stop if the first physical replay fails exact-state gate; do not tune physical parameters or alter the biological decoder to achieve a sign. A and B remain rivals for a separately budgeted full-organism campaign after this inexpensive discriminant.
